heard: The sun is not actually on fire. Picture a campfire, then a forest fire the size of Earth. Neither could burn in space without any oxygen. Arthur Eddington proposed in 1920 that stars run on fusion. Nuclear fusion crushes hydrogen into helium at 15 million Kelvin. But the reaction in the solar core is surprisingly sluggish. One cubic meter of that core generates just 276 watts. That's less volumetric heat than a resting human body. You're technically a more efficient heater than the sun. Our star is simply too big to be on fire.
